comparison: Perfect agreement on whole-cell electrophysiology demonstrating NaChBac mechanosensitivity (C2, C3, C34-C43, C96-C97). Both evaluations find the shear stress experiments and comparison to NaV1.5 convincing and well-controlled.

Strong agreement on single-channel evidence for mechanosensitivity (C4, C45-C52, C54-C56, C102). Both evaluations accept the voltage-dependent, pressure-dependent, and reversible changes in PO. Note: Peer review does not include C53 in this result.

Disagreement on reversibility claim C53 for NaV1.5. OpenEval includes C53 in supported single-channel findings, while peer reviewers specifically requested additional verification for NaV1.5 reversibility (essential revision #3), marking it as uncertain.

Strong agreement on mechanistic interpretation (C57-C62, C100-C101, C103). Both evaluations accept that force modifies existing transitions rather than creating new states, and that voltage-dependence of mechanosensitivity is convincing. Peer review also includes C110-C111 in this supported interpretation.

Agreement on kinetic modeling approach distinguishing MSO from MSA models (C5, C63-C68, C74-C75, C104-C107). Both find the modeling rigorous and convincing, though peer review notes the mechanism is identical to established Kv channel mechanisms.

Significant disagreement on closed dwell time distribution claims (C69-C73, C108-C109). OpenEval finds these claims supported by the data, while peer reviewers explicitly challenged the shift in closed lifetimes (essential revision #5), stating the distributions do not show obvious divergence.

Disagreement on structural interpretation claims (C7, C80-C84, C113-C116). OpenEval finds the S6 displacement analysis and connection to force-from-lipid model well-supported, while peer reviewers requested these structural claims be 'more strongly supported or substantially softened,' viewing them as speculative.

Disagreement on mutagenesis interpretation (C8, C85-C91, C117-C120). OpenEval finds the I228G and pore mutation data strongly support the MSO model, while peer reviewers expressed substantial concerns about I228G interpretation, noting 'multiple interpretations are plausible' and the logic remains unclear.

Agreement that main conclusions are speculative regarding broader implications (C9, C145-C146). OpenEval marks these as well-supported synthesis but notes C10, C112, C125, C147 are speculative. Peer reviewers requested evolutionary and eukaryotic extrapolations be softened or removed.

Agreement on speculative nature of extrapolations to eukaryotic channels (C10, C112, C125, C147). OpenEval explicitly marks these as uncertain/speculative, and peer reviewers requested these claims be substantially softened.

Strong agreement on force-from-lipid theoretical framework (C126-C136). Both evaluations accept this established background knowledge without challenge, viewing it as appropriate context for interpreting results.

Agreement that physiological relevance claims are speculative (C137-C142, C144). OpenEval notes these represent contextual discussion with C144 being speculative, while peer reviewers requested physiological relevance claims be better supported or softened.
Agreement on NaChBac as appropriate model system (C1, C28-C33). Both evaluations accept the rationale for using the bacterial channel without challenge, viewing it as well-supported background.
Agreement on background and rationale (C11-C27). Both evaluations accept this contextual information as well-supported by prior work, establishing appropriate scientific context.

Disagreement on methodological claims about tension measurements (C149-C150). OpenEval finds these appropriately documented, while peer reviewers raised concerns about physiological relevance of patch tensions and requested clarification on shear force tension calculations (essential revisions #2 and #4).
Agreement on P1KO cell methodology (C148). Both evaluations accept this technical detail without challenge.
Agreement on consistency with prior work (C121-C122). Both evaluations affirm the findings are consistent with established models, viewing this positively.
Agreement on consistency with prior Kv channel work (C98-C99, C124). Both evaluations accept the parallel findings with established mechanisms.
Minor overlap on C123 regarding mechanosensitive pore opening. OpenEval includes this in supported mutagenesis findings, while peer reviewers requested evolutionary speculation be toned down.
Minor overlap on background claims (C92-C95). OpenEval views these as supported background, while peer reviewers grouped them with physiological relevance claims requiring softening.
Minor overlap on C76 regarding structural context. OpenEval includes this in structural analysis findings, while peer reviewers accept the force-from-lipid framework without challenge.
Minor overlap on C143 regarding lipid-protein interactions. OpenEval views this as supported background, while peer reviewers grouped it with physiological relevance requiring better support.
Minor overlap on C110-C111 regarding model predictions. OpenEval includes these in comprehensive kinetic modeling support, while peer reviewers accept the mechanistic interpretation.
Minor overlap on C147 regarding physiological implications. OpenEval marks this as speculative extrapolation, while peer reviewers requested physiological relevance claims be softened.
